item.title: Obernolte-Trahan artificial intelligence bill introduced in House
item.description:
# Obernolte-Trahan artificial intelligence bill introduced in House 07/23/2026 11:40 AM EDT
Two key House lawmakers introduced an [artificial intelligence bill](https://legislation.politicopro.com/bill/US_119_HR_9925) Thursday that would preempt some state AI laws and give the government the ability to restrict deployment of models determined to pose catastrophic risks, according to three people familiar with the proposal.
Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) and Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.), follows a [discussion draft unveiled last month](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/04/obernolte-trahan-ai-bill-lands-on-the-hill-00949920).
It represents the latest bipartisan attempt to establish a federal framework for AI governance after Congress has repeatedly failed to advance broad legislation.
But it includes specific carveouts to allow state laws to regulate the deployment of AI and child safety, among others.
Bill cosponsors include Reps. Scott Peters (D-Calif.), Scott Franklin (R-Fla.), Suhas Subramanyan (D-Va.) and Erin Houchin (R-Ind.).

item.title: Katy ISD launches artificial intelligence framework for 2026-27 school year | Katy - Fulshear
item.description:
# Katy ISD launches artificial intelligence framework for 2026-27 school year Katy ISD's new artificial intelligence framework is going live in the 2026-27 school year.
Bell said Katy ISD’s AI framework will go into effect in the 2026-27 school year and outlines how students come in contact with AI in and out of school.
“So it’s here, it’s in our students hands, they’re using it, it’s changing how people work, how they create [and] communicate.”
Katy ISD’s goal is to expose students to consistent, intentional AI use across all campuses, while not getting in the way of learning and teaching.
- Seventh grade is allowed to use district-approved AI tools under teacher supervision, but can not use non-approved generative AI tools on school devices or networks. - Eighth through 12th grades are permitted to use generative AI tools for specific educational purposes with teacher authorization, but they must follow district policies and cite AI when appropriate.
